md_description: This DAG represents a corrected experimental and computational workflow for evaluating genomic stability in donor-derived iPSC lines across multiple culture conditions. It includes culture conditioning, SNP array and whole-genome sequencing measurements at multiple passages, phenotype observation, computational derivation of aberration calls, and final integration into a metadata table used for comparative assessment of condition-dependent genomic stability.

ipsc_lines.reasoning: This is an Entity node, so I included only intrinsic identity and origin fields for the donor-derived iPSC starting material. I excluded culture protocol, passage handling, sequencing/capture settings, raw file properties, aberration calls, and phenotype outcomes because those belong to downstream Process/Capture/Signal/Derivative nodes. Because this is the root biological material, I also included donor and line identifiers plus donor-demographic/origin descriptors needed to distinguish lines, while avoiding any fields already generated elsewhere in the DAG (none provided here) and avoiding repetition of downstream condition or assay metadata.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for each iPSC line in the study, assigned at the root material level before any culture or assay steps; use a stable string format such as 'iPSC_D01_L03'.

Identifier linking the iPSC line to its source donor; use a stable string format such as 'D001'. This is recorded once for the starting biological material and is not repeated on downstream process or assay nodes.

Age of the donor at the time the original somatic cell source was collected, recorded as a numeric value in years; typical range in this study depends on donor cohort and should reflect the source material only.
Biological sex of the source donor at collection time for the original cell source. This describes the intrinsic donor context of the iPSC line, not culture state.
Self-reported or recorded donor ancestry/ethnicity category associated with the source material, used as intrinsic provenance metadata for the iPSC line.
Original somatic cell type used to generate the iPSC line, recorded at derivation of the starting biological material; examples include fibroblast, peripheral_blood_mononuclear_cell, or keratinocyte.

Free-text description of the donor-derived starting material and any provenance details relevant to line identity, such as tissue source, reprogramming origin, or cohort notes; record only intrinsic source information, not culture handling.

Method used to generate the iPSC line from the original donor cell source, recorded as the derivation method of the entity; examples include integrating_viral, non_integrating_sendai, episomal, or mrna_based.
Whether the iPSC line was established as a clonal line derived from a single reprogrammed clone versus a mixed population; record as true when the entity is a clonal line.

Baseline karyotype or gross chromosomal integrity status of the iPSC line at establishment or receipt, before the culture-condition workflow begins; record as a categorical provenance attribute such as normal or abnormal.

culture_condition_application.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the protocol parameters and active handling settings used to apply the culture conditions to the iPSC lines. I excluded donor identity, starting cell provenance, downstream assay/capture settings, raw file properties, and computed aberration/phenotype outputs because those belong to Entity, Capture, Signal, or Derivative nodes. The fields focus on the condition regime itself: media supplements, oxygen tension, passaging technique, duration, passaging frequency, and the operator/lab handling context needed to reproduce the maintenance step. No prior generated fields were provided for this DAG, so there was no overlap to avoid beyond staying within process territory.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the applied culture-condition regime used during iPSC maintenance; use a stable string format such as 'CC_01'. This identifies the process instance, not the resulting cell line.
Base culture medium used during maintenance of the iPSC lines, recorded at the time the culture condition is applied; examples include mTeSR1, Essential 8, or similar stem-cell medium formulations.

Key media supplements added during the culture condition application, recorded as the protocol-defined supplement set used for the maintenance step; examples include bfgf, tgfbeta_inhibitor, or roscovitine. Use a controlled categorical label or protocol-specific free-text naming convention if not among the listed values.
Configured oxygen concentration used during culture maintenance, measured as the incubator or chamber setpoint applied to the iPSC cultures at the time of exposure; typical range is 1-21 percent.

Passaging method used to expand and maintain the iPSC lines under the specified condition, recorded as the active handling technique applied during the process step; examples include enzymatic dissociation, manual picking, or EDTA-based passaging.
Number of days between routine passages while the culture condition is being applied, recorded as the maintenance cadence for this process step; typical values are in the range of 1-14 days.

Total duration for which the iPSC lines were maintained under the specified condition regime during this process step, measured in days from initiation to transfer to downstream measurement; typical range depends on experimental design.

Passage number of the iPSC culture at the end of the condition application period, recorded as the state of the culture immediately before downstream capture or transfer; use an integer such as 10, 15, or 20.
Configured incubator temperature used during maintenance of the iPSC cultures, measured as the instrument setpoint applied throughout the process step; typical value is around 37.0 degrees Celsius.
Role of the person or team performing the culture-condition application, recorded to capture who executed the process step; examples include researcher, technician, or automated_system.

treated_ipsc_lines.reasoning: This is an Entity node representing the conditioned iPSC material after the culture process and before any downstream capture. I included only state/provenance fields intrinsic to the treated lines, such as lineage linkage to the starting material, applied condition identity, passage state at harvest, and whether the culture was considered viable/usable for downstream assays. I excluded process parameters (media, oxygen, passaging technique) because those belong to the upstream Process node, and I excluded capture, signal, and derivative details because those belong downstream. I also avoided repeating any root identity fields that would already exist on the initial iPSC entity unless needed here as a linkage or post-treatment state descriptor.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the conditioned iPSC line or culture batch after exposure to the culture regime and before downstream measurements; use a stable string format such as 'TREATED_D01_L03_P10'.
Identifier of the originating donor iPSC line from which this treated entity was produced; use the same stable line identifier format as the root material to preserve lineage linkage.
Identifier of the culture-condition regime applied to this treated iPSC entity, linking it to the upstream maintenance process; use a stable string format such as 'CC_01'.
Passage number of the iPSC line immediately after the culture-condition exposure period and before downstream capture; record as an integer such as 8, 10, or 15.
Total number of days the iPSC line was exposed to the specified culture condition before downstream measurement; measure in days from the start of the condition regimen to harvest for capture.
Qualitative state of the treated iPSC culture at the point it is handed off to downstream capture, describing whether the culture was suitable for measurement.
Whether the conditioned iPSC culture remained viable and usable after the exposure period and before downstream assays; record the status assessed at harvest.
Batch identifier for the treated culture preparation, used when multiple replicate cultures are exposed under the same condition; use a stable string format such as 'BATCH_02'.
Date and time when the conditioned iPSC material was collected and transferred to downstream capture, recorded at the end of the treatment step.

snp_array_capture.reasoning: This is a Capture node, so I included only the measurement-session and instrument-configuration fields for the SNP array assay. I focused on the actively controlled hardware/setup details needed to reproduce the capture: platform configuration, chip array type, hybridization/scanning settings, and measurement batch/run identifiers. I excluded sample provenance and culture-condition details because those belong to the upstream Entity/Process nodes, and I excluded file format, raw intensity sizes, and call-quality outputs because those belong to the downstream Signal node. I also avoided any computational aberration interpretation, since that is reserved for the Process and Derivative nodes after capture.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the SNP array measurement session performed on a conditioned iPSC sample at a selected passage; use a stable string format such as 'SNP_CAP_01'.

Configured SNP array instrument platform used for the capture session, describing the manufacturer/platform family actively employed for genomic integrity measurement; example is the Affymetrix CytoScan HD platform.
Chip or array formulation used for the SNP capture session, recorded as the specific assay consumable loaded onto the instrument during measurement; example is CytoScan HD array.

Duration of the DNA hybridization step used in the SNP array capture workflow, measured in hours and recorded as the instrument/protocol setting applied for this session; typical range is approximately 12-24 hours.
Scanner hardware model used to read out the SNP array after hybridization, recorded as the instrument model actively configured for the capture session.

Scanner resolution used during SNP array readout, measured in microns per pixel or equivalent instrument setting; report the configured value applied to this session, typically within submicron to few-micron range.
Version or identifier of the post-hybridization wash protocol used during the SNP capture session, recorded as the instrument/protocol setting applied before scanning.
Date and time when the SNP array measurement run was initiated on the instrument, recorded for the capture session at the point of data acquisition.

Role of the person or system that performed the SNP array capture session, used to describe who configured and executed the measurement run; examples include researcher, technician, or automated_system.

snp_raw_signal.reasoning: This is a Signal node, so I included only raw data artefact descriptors for the SNP array output: file format, file size, matrix dimensions, technical quality indicators, and storage location. I excluded capture settings such as platform, scan resolution, and hybridization protocol because those belong to the upstream Capture node. I also excluded preprocessing, aberration interpretation, and any biologically meaningful calls because those belong to downstream Process/Derivative nodes. No prior generated fields were provided for this DAG beyond earlier nodes, so I ensured the names stay specific to raw SNP signal properties without duplicating capture or analysis metadata.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the raw SNP array signal artefact produced from one capture session; use a stable string format such as 'SNP_SIG_01'.
File format of the raw SNP array output at the point of storage or export, recorded as a technical artefact property; examples include idat, cel, or text-based matrix exports.
Size of the raw SNP array data file in bytes, measured after acquisition and storage of the artefact; typical values depend on platform and export format.
Number of probes or rows represented in the raw SNP signal file or matrix, recorded as a technical dimension of the artefact.
Number of sample channels, intensity channels, or columns represented in the raw SNP signal file or matrix, recorded as a technical dimension of the artefact.
Storage location or URI where the raw SNP array signal file is archived, recorded as the file path or repository pointer for the artefact; example format is a local path or object-store URI.
Whether the raw SNP signal file passed technical integrity checks at storage or ingestion time, such as checksum validation or successful file parsing; this is a raw artefact quality flag only.
Technical signal-to-noise ratio reported for the raw SNP array artefact, measured after acquisition as a quality metric of the file or matrix; typical values are platform- and pipeline-dependent.
Proportion of missing or uncalled entries in the raw SNP signal artefact, measured as a technical quality metric of the file or matrix after acquisition; value is typically between 0 and 1.
Checksum or hash value used to verify the integrity of the stored raw SNP array file, recorded as a technical provenance field for the signal artefact.

wgs_capture.reasoning: I corrected the collision by removing capture_operator_role, since it had already been generated for a previous DAG step and must not be repeated. The remaining fields stay within the Capture node’s territory by describing WGS instrument/session configuration only: sequencer hardware, chemistry, library prep, read layout, target depth, flowcell identifier, and run timing. I excluded sample provenance, raw file properties, and downstream analysis outputs because those belong to other node types.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the whole-genome sequencing measurement session performed on a conditioned iPSC sample at a selected passage; use a stable string format such as 'WGS_CAP_01'.
Sequencing instrument model used for the WGS capture session, recorded as the hardware actively configured for data acquisition; example is Illumina NovaSeq 6000.
Sequencing chemistry or reagent kit version used on the instrument during the WGS capture session, recorded as the configured readout chemistry for this run.
Library preparation method used before sequencing, recorded as the capture-session configuration for WGS; examples include PCR-free genomic DNA library prep or standard paired-end prep.
Configured read length in base pairs for each WGS read, measured as the sequencing setup applied during the capture session; typical values are 100-250 bp.
Sequencing layout used for the WGS capture session, recorded as the active read configuration on the instrument.

Intended mean genome coverage depth for the WGS run, measured as the planned sequencing depth at the time of capture setup; typical values are in the range of 10x to 60x or higher depending on study design.
Identifier of the flow cell or sequencing cartridge used for the WGS capture session, recorded as the instrument consumable loaded for the run; use a stable string format such as 'FC12345'.
Date and time when the WGS run was initiated on the sequencer, recorded at the point of data acquisition for the capture session.

wgs_raw_reads.reasoning: This is a Signal node, so I included only raw-read artefact descriptors for the WGS output: file format, file size, read counts, read length distribution, storage location, and technical integrity/quality metrics. I excluded capture-session settings such as sequencer model, chemistry, and coverage because those belong to the upstream Capture node. I also excluded alignment, variant calling, and biological interpretation because those belong to downstream Process and Derivative nodes. I avoided the previously generated field name 'capture_operator_role' entirely and kept the schema limited to raw data properties of the sequencing artefact.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the raw WGS read artefact produced from one sequencing capture session; use a stable string format such as 'WGS_SIG_01'.

File format of the raw whole-genome sequencing reads at the point of storage or export, recorded as a technical artefact property; examples include fastq, bam, or cram depending on the stage captured as raw output.
Size of the raw WGS read file in bytes, measured after acquisition and storage of the artefact; typical values vary widely with coverage and format.
Total number of reads represented in the raw WGS artefact, recorded as a technical dimension of the sequencing file or dataset.
Mean read length in base pairs for the raw WGS reads, measured from the stored artefact after acquisition; typical values reflect the configured sequencing chemistry and read mode.
Storage location or URI where the raw WGS read file is archived, recorded as the file path or repository pointer for the artefact; example format is a local path or object-store URI.
Whether the raw WGS read file passed technical integrity checks at storage or ingestion time, such as checksum validation or successful parsing; this is a raw artefact quality flag only.
Proportion of bases in the raw WGS artefact with Phred quality score at or above Q30, recorded as a technical quality metric of the raw data file; typical values range from 0 to 1.
Proportion of reads or bases showing adapter contamination in the raw WGS artefact, recorded as a technical quality metric after acquisition; typical values range from 0 to 1.
Checksum or hash value used to verify the integrity of the stored raw WGS file, recorded as a technical provenance field for the signal artefact.

snp_processing.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only computational analysis parameters and software-agent details for transforming raw SNP signal into aberration calls. I focused on the processing method, reference genome/build, normalization and segmentation settings, QC thresholds, and the software package/version/repository used, because those are the active settings that define how the transformation was performed. I excluded raw signal properties because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded the resulting copy-number or aberration calls because those belong to the downstream Derivative node. I also avoided any donor- or culture-level fields, and I did not repeat previously generated field names from earlier steps in this DAG.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the SNP array analysis process instance that transforms raw SNP signal into aberration calls; use a stable string format such as 'SNP_PROC_01'.
Name of the analysis pipeline used to process the raw SNP array data into copy-number and aberration inferences; examples include an R/Bioconductor-based workflow or a vendor analysis suite.
Version of the SNP array analysis pipeline used for processing, recorded at the time the raw signal is converted into calls; use a software version string such as '1.2.3'.
Repository URL or source location for the analysis pipeline implementation used in this process step, recorded to support reproducibility; examples include a GitHub or GitLab URL.
Reference genome build used during SNP array processing, recorded as the aligned coordinate framework for normalization and aberration inference; examples include hg19 or hg38.
Normalization method applied to the raw SNP array signal before segmentation or aberration calling, recorded as the computational setting used for this process step.
Segmentation algorithm used to infer copy-number regions from normalized SNP signal, recorded as the active method applied in this process step; examples include CBS or HMM-based segmentation.

Quality-control threshold used to accept or reject SNP array data during processing, measured as the configured cutoff for this analysis step; the exact metric should be documented in the description accompanying the chosen threshold.
Minimum number of probes required for a segmented region to be retained as a candidate copy-number event during SNP array processing; recorded as the process parameter used for filtering.
Date and time when the SNP array processing run started, recorded for the computational transformation step that generates aberration calls from raw signal.
Date and time when the SNP array processing run finished, recorded for the computational transformation step that generates aberration calls from raw signal.

snp_aberration_calls.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only computed-result fields that describe the SNP-derived aberration calls themselves: call identifiers, event type, genomic coordinates, copy-number state, event size, confidence/support, and summary-level quality indicators for the derived output. I excluded raw signal properties because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded processing parameters such as normalization, segmentation, or software because those belong to the upstream Process node. I also did not include donor/culture provenance or capture settings, since this node represents the computed aberration output only. I avoided previously generated field names from earlier nodes and kept the schema focused on the downstream, analysis-ready result.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for a single SNP-derived aberration call, produced by the processing step that converts raw SNP signal into computed genomic events; use a stable string format such as 'SNP_ABR_0001'.

Identifier of the SNP array processing run that generated this aberration call, used to link the derivative result back to the computational process instance; use a stable string format such as 'SNP_PROC_01'.
Type of genomic event called from the SNP array data, recorded as the computed result category for this derivative; examples include copy_number_gain, copy_number_loss, or loss_of_heterozygosity.
Chromosome on which the SNP-derived aberration is located, recorded as the computed genomic coordinate context for the call; use chromosome labels such as 1-22, X, or Y.
Start coordinate in base pairs for the aberrant genomic interval inferred from the SNP array analysis, measured on the reference genome build used in processing.
End coordinate in base pairs for the aberrant genomic interval inferred from the SNP array analysis, measured on the reference genome build used in processing.
Inferred copy-number state for the called segment, recorded as the computed ploidy-like output of the derivative step; examples include 0, 1, 2, 3, or 4+ depending on the caller.
Size of the aberrant segment in megabases, computed from the start and end coordinates of the derivative call; typical values depend on the size of the detected event.
Confidence or posterior support score assigned to the aberration call by the derivative algorithm, recorded as the computed reliability metric for this event; scale depends on the analysis method.
Number of SNP array probes supporting the aberration call, recorded as a computed evidence metric for the derivative result; higher counts generally indicate stronger support.
Whether the aberration call met the study's reporting criteria after derivation, recorded as a downstream result flag indicating inclusion in the analysis-ready output.

wgs_processing.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the computational transformation settings used to align WGS reads and call variants/structural changes. I focused on software/configuration fields for alignment, variant calling, structural variant calling, duplicate marking, base-quality recalibration, and filtering thresholds. I excluded raw read file properties because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded the resulting variant calls because those belong to the downstream Derivative node. I also removed fields that collided with previously generated DAG-wide names, specifically reference_genome_build, processing_start_datetime, and processing_end_datetime, and replaced them with WGS-specific non-colliding equivalents.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the WGS analysis process instance that transforms raw reads into variant and structural change calls; use a stable string format such as 'WGS_PROC_01'.
Name of the software used to align WGS reads to the reference genome in this process step; examples include BWA-MEM or Bowtie2.
Version of the alignment software used in the WGS processing step, recorded for reproducibility; use a software version string such as '0.7.17'.
Name of the software used to call small sequence variants from aligned WGS reads in this process step; examples include GATK or FreeBayes.
Version of the small-variant calling software used in the WGS processing step, recorded for reproducibility; use a software version string such as '4.4.0'.
Name of the software used to detect structural genomic changes from WGS data in this process step; examples include Manta, DELLY, or LUMPY.
Version of the structural-variant calling software used in the WGS processing step, recorded for reproducibility; use a software version string such as '1.6.0'.
Reference genome build used for read alignment and downstream variant analysis, recorded as the coordinate framework for this WGS processing step; examples include hg19 or hg38.
Method used to identify or mark duplicate reads before variant analysis, recorded as the processing setting applied to aligned WGS data.
Method used to recalibrate base quality scores prior to variant calling, recorded as the process configuration used for WGS analysis.
Minimum allele fraction required for a sequence variant to be retained during WGS processing, measured as the caller filtering threshold; typical values are between 0 and 1.

Minimum mapping quality threshold applied to aligned reads before variant and structural event calling, recorded as the filtering cutoff for this process step; typical values are integer Phred-scale scores.
Date and time when the WGS processing run started, recorded for the computational transformation of reads into genomic calls; use an ISO 8601 timestamp string such as '2026-08-18T14:30:00Z'.
Date and time when the WGS processing run finished, recorded for the computational transformation of reads into genomic calls; use an ISO 8601 timestamp string such as '2026-08-18T16:45:00Z'.

wgs_genomic_calls.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I kept only computed WGS call outputs and removed colliding field names that were already used elsewhere in the DAG: chromosome, start_position_bp, and end_position_bp. To avoid duplication while preserving the derivative semantics, I replaced them with WGS-specific names for locus representation and retained call identity, variant class, allele/genotype attributes, evidence/support, and quality metrics. I excluded raw data and process settings because those belong upstream, and I did not include any sample provenance or capture metadata.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for a single WGS-derived genomic call, produced by the process that analyzes aligned reads; use a stable string format such as 'WGS_VAR_0001'.
Identifier of the WGS processing run that generated this genomic call, used to link the derivative result back to the computational process instance; use a stable string format such as 'WGS_PROC_01'.
Class of genomic variant called from WGS data, recorded as the computed result category for this derivative; examples include snv, indel, or structural_variant.
Genomic locus label for the WGS-derived variant, recorded as the computed coordinate context for the call in a single string representation such as 'chr7:140453136-140453136'.
Reference allele reported for the WGS-derived single-nucleotide or small indel call, recorded as part of the computed genomic event representation.
Alternate allele reported for the WGS-derived single-nucleotide or small indel call, recorded as part of the computed genomic event representation.
Genotype assigned to the genomic variant call, recorded as the computed sample-level interpretation such as homozygous reference, heterozygous, or homozygous alternate.
Observed allele fraction supporting the called variant in the processed WGS data, recorded as a computed evidence metric; typical values are between 0 and 1.
Quality or confidence score assigned to the WGS variant call by the derivative algorithm, recorded as the computed reliability metric for this event; scale depends on the analysis method.
Number of aligned reads supporting the WGS-derived variant call, recorded as a computed evidence metric for the derivative result.
Whether the WGS variant call passed the analysis-specific downstream filtering criteria, recorded as the final call-level quality flag for the derivative result.

Name of the downstream reporting or annotation tool used to represent the final WGS genomic call output, if applicable; use only if the derivative step emits a tool-labeled call record distinct from the upstream process.

phenotype_capture.reasoning: This is a Capture node, so I included only the direct observation-session and instrument/configuration fields for phenotype recording. I focused on how the phenotype was observed and documented: assay/imaging modality, microscope or observer setup, magnification, capture date/time, and observation context. I excluded culture-condition provenance because that belongs upstream, and I excluded summarized phenotype outputs because those belong downstream on the Signal and Derivative nodes. I also avoided previously generated field names that collided across the DAG, especially not reusing generic position or chromosome terms. The resulting schema is limited to the measurement session for phenotype observation rather than the biology or the computed summary.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the phenotype observation session performed on conditioned iPSC lines; use a stable string format such as 'PHENO_CAP_01'.

Method used to observe and record phenotype in the conditioned iPSC lines during this capture session; examples include brightfield microscopy, phase-contrast microscopy, or immunofluorescence imaging.
Microscope or imaging system model used to record phenotype observations, if imaging was performed; record the instrument actively configured for the capture session.
Objective magnification used during phenotype capture, recorded as the imaging configuration applied for this session; typical values might be 10x, 20x, or 40x.
Number of imaging channels or recorded observation channels used during phenotype capture, measured as a technical setting of the observation session.
Date and time when the phenotype observation was performed, recorded at the point of direct capture from the conditioned iPSC lines.
Role of the person or system performing the phenotype capture, used to identify who configured and executed the observation; examples include researcher, technician, or automated_system.

Physical location or laboratory area where the phenotype observation was performed, recorded as the session context for the capture event; example formats include room labels or instrument station names.

Exposure time used for imaging-based phenotype capture, measured in milliseconds and recorded as the active acquisition setting for this session; typical values depend on the modality and signal intensity.
Focus strategy used during phenotype observation, recorded as the capture setting for image acquisition or manual review; examples include auto_focus, manual_focus, or z_stack_based.

phenotype_signal.reasoning: This is a Signal node, so I included only raw phenotype artefact descriptors: file format, file size, image dimensions or observation count, storage location, and technical quality/integrity metrics. I excluded observation settings such as microscope model, magnification, and exposure time because those belong to the upstream Capture node. I also excluded phenotype summaries or biological interpretation because those belong to downstream Process and Derivative nodes. I kept the schema centered on the raw recorded observation file(s) or table(s) produced by phenotype capture, and avoided previously generated field names from other DAG steps.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the raw phenotype observation artefact produced from one capture session; use a stable string format such as 'PHENO_SIG_01'.
File format of the raw phenotype observation output at the point of storage or export, recorded as a technical artefact property; examples include tiff, jpeg, png, csv, or json.
Size of the raw phenotype signal file in bytes, measured after acquisition and storage of the artefact; typical values vary by image count, resolution, and format.
Number of image frames, fields of view, or observation records represented in the raw phenotype artefact, recorded as a technical dimension of the signal.
Image height in pixels for the raw phenotype artefact when the signal is image-based; if the signal is tabular text, record the corresponding observation matrix height as a technical dimension.
Image width in pixels for the raw phenotype artefact when the signal is image-based; if the signal is tabular text, record the corresponding observation matrix width as a technical dimension.
Storage location or URI where the raw phenotype observation file is archived, recorded as the file path or repository pointer for the artefact; example format is a local path or object-store URI.
Whether the raw phenotype observation file passed technical integrity checks at storage or ingestion time, such as checksum validation or successful parsing; this is a raw artefact quality flag only.
Technical blur or sharpness metric for image-based phenotype artefacts, measured after acquisition as a raw-data quality indicator; value scale depends on the imaging system.
Checksum or hash value used to verify the integrity of the stored raw phenotype observation file, recorded as a technical provenance field for the signal artefact.

phenotype_summary_process.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only computational aggregation settings that transform raw phenotype signals into a summary table. I focused on the summary method, software agent, grouping level, scoring scheme, thresholds, and output-normalization choices that define how the aggregation was performed. I excluded raw image/observation properties because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded the resulting phenotype summary metrics because those belong to the downstream Derivative node. I also avoided donor, culture, and capture fields, since this node describes the computation over phenotype data rather than the biological material or the original observation session.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the phenotype summarization process instance that aggregates raw observation data into a computable summary; use a stable string format such as 'PHENO_PROC_01'.
Name of the software or library used to aggregate phenotype observations into summary form; examples include Python/pandas or R/tidyverse.
Version of the summarization software or library used in this process step, recorded for reproducibility; use a software version string such as '2.1.0'.

Level at which phenotype observations are aggregated during summarization, recorded as the grouping unit used for comparison across conditions; examples include per_sample, per_line, per_condition, or per_passage.

Method used to convert raw phenotype observations into summary scores or labels, recorded as the computational rule applied during this process step; examples include manual_curation, rule_based_scoring, or model_based_scoring.
Method used to identify or exclude outlier phenotype observations before summarization, recorded as the filtering strategy used in this process step.
Normalization method used to make phenotype summaries comparable across culture conditions or batches, recorded as the process setting applied during aggregation.

Minimum number of raw phenotype observations required for a group to be summarized, recorded as the process-level inclusion threshold; typical values depend on the number of replicates and fields of view.
Date and time when phenotype summarization began, recorded for the computational aggregation step.
Date and time when phenotype summarization completed, recorded for the computational aggregation step.

phenotype_summary.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only computed phenotype-summary outputs rather than raw observations or summarization parameters. I focused on the summarized result fields needed for downstream comparison across conditions: summary identifier, link to the processing run, phenotype category, direction/magnitude of change, counts, prevalence, and overall summary confidence. I excluded capture-session details and raw signal properties because those belong upstream, and I excluded the summarization algorithm/settings because those belong to the upstream Process node. I also avoided repeating any previously generated field names from earlier steps in the DAG.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the computed phenotype summary record derived from raw phenotype observations; use a stable string format such as 'PHENO_SUM_0001'.

Identifier of the phenotype summarization process run that generated this summary record, used to link the derivative result back to the computational process instance; use a stable string format such as 'PHENO_PROC_01'.

Phenotype class represented in the computed summary, recorded as the biological feature being summarized; examples include morphology_change, growth_arrest, differentiation_like_state, cell_death, or other observed changes.
Direction of the observed phenotype relative to the baseline conditioned or untreated state, recorded as the computed summary direction for comparison across culture conditions.
Numeric score representing the magnitude or severity of the summarized phenotype, computed from the aggregated observations; the scale depends on the summary method used.
Number of raw phenotype observations contributing to this summary record, recorded as the computed support size for the derivative output.
Fraction of samples or observations within the group showing the phenotype represented by this summary, measured as a value between 0 and 1.
Confidence or reliability score assigned to the computed phenotype summary, recorded as the downstream quality metric for the derivative result; scale depends on the aggregation method.
Whether the summarized phenotype was judged to be associated with the applied culture condition in the downstream interpretation of the observation set.
Human-readable label for the computed phenotype summary, such as 'abnormal_morphology_high' or 'normal_growth_low'; use only if the derivative output emits a compact categorical label.

integrated_metadata_process.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only integration/composition fields that describe how separate upstream results are merged into a single table. I focused on the integration software agent and merge strategy, join keys, row-granularity, conflict-resolution rules, and output schema/version because those define the transformation performed on the incoming SNP/WGS/phenotype derivatives. I excluded the actual donor, culture, and assay measurements because those belong to upstream nodes, and I excluded the final table contents because those belong to the downstream Derivative node. I also avoided field names already generated in prior steps, including the generic processing timestamps and reference genome build fields that were previously used elsewhere in the DAG.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the metadata integration process that merges culture protocol details, genomic results, and phenotype results into one analysis-ready table; use a stable string format such as 'INT_PROC_01'.
Name of the software or library used to merge the upstream data sources into the integrated metadata table; examples include Python/pandas or R/dplyr.
Version of the integration software or library used for merging, recorded for reproducibility; use a software version string such as '2.2.0'.

Strategy used to combine upstream records into the integrated metadata table, recorded as the process rule used for joining rows across sources; examples include one_to_one, one_to_many, or many_to_one joins.

Primary join key or keys used to align culture, genomic, and phenotype records during integration, recorded as the metadata fields used for row matching; examples include line ID, condition ID, and passage number.
Granularity of each output row in the integrated table after merging, recorded as the unit of analysis used for the final table; examples include per_line, per_condition, per_passage, or per_sample.

Rule used when upstream sources contain conflicting values for a shared key or attribute during integration, recorded as the process-level resolution policy; examples include prioritize_latest, prioritize_manual_review, or preserve_all.
Method used to handle missing fields during table integration, recorded as the process rule for incomplete upstream records; examples include leave_blank, impute, or drop_row.
Version identifier for the integrated metadata table schema produced by this process, recorded to track changes in column structure or naming across runs; use a stable string format such as 'v1.0'.
Date and time when the metadata integration run started or was executed, recorded for the process step that creates the final analysis-ready table.

integrated_metadata_table.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only fields that describe the final integrated table as a computed output: table identity, output schema/version, row and column counts, included source components, linkage completeness, and overall table-level quality flags. I excluded donor/culture/assay specifics because those belong to upstream Entity, Process, Capture, Signal, and earlier Derivative nodes, and I excluded integration algorithm settings because those belong to the upstream Process node. I also avoided any field names already generated elsewhere in the DAG, including generic identifiers and timestamps. The goal here is to characterize the final analysis-ready artifact itself, not the details of the inputs used to create it.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the final analysis-ready metadata table produced by the integration process; use a stable string format such as 'META_TABLE_01'.

Identifier of the metadata integration process that generated this table, used to link the derivative output back to the computational process instance; use a stable string format such as 'INT_PROC_01'.
Version identifier for the final integrated table schema, recorded as the structure of the computed output at the time of generation; use a stable string format such as 'v1.0'.
Number of rows in the final integrated metadata table, measured after the integration process completes; this is a technical dimension of the derivative table output.
Number of columns in the final integrated metadata table, measured after the integration process completes; this is a technical dimension of the derivative table output.

List or compact description of the upstream data components included in the final table, such as donor context, culture protocol details, SNP aberration calls, WGS variant calls, and phenotype summaries; this describes the composition of the derivative output.

Fraction of expected upstream records successfully represented in the final integrated table, measured as a value between 0 and 1 after integration; higher values indicate fewer missing joins or dropped rows.

Proportion of records that could not be linked across upstream sources during table construction, recorded as a table-level quality metric for the derivative output; value is typically between 0 and 1.
Number of duplicate rows detected in the final integrated table after merging, recorded as a table-quality metric for the derivative output.
Whether the integrated table passed the criteria for being considered analysis-ready, recorded as a final table-level quality flag for downstream comparative analysis.

Storage location or URI where the final integrated metadata table is archived, recorded as the file path or repository pointer for the derivative artifact; example format is a local path or object-store URI.
Checksum or hash value used to verify the integrity of the final integrated metadata table, recorded as a technical provenance field for the derivative artifact.

comparative_analysis.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the analysis settings used to compare integrated metadata across culture conditions and derive stability outcomes. I focused on the statistical/computational agent, comparison design, grouping factors, model type, multiple-testing correction, significance thresholds, and optimization objective, because those define how the transformation was performed. I excluded raw donor, culture, capture, signal, and derivative content because those belong upstream, and I excluded the final comparative findings because those belong to the downstream Derivative node. I also avoided any previously generated field names in the DAG, including generic processing timestamps and genome-build fields, to prevent collisions.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the comparative analysis process that evaluates culture-condition effects on genomic stability using the integrated metadata table; use a stable string format such as 'COMP_PROC_01'.
Name of the software or library used for the comparative stability analysis; examples include Python/scipy, R, or a statistical modeling package.
Version of the statistical or computational software used in this process step, recorded for reproducibility; use a software version string such as '1.0.0'.

Primary factor used to compare stability outcomes across the integrated table, recorded as the grouping variable or predictor examined in the analysis; examples include culture_condition, oxygen_tension, media_supplement, or passaging_technique.

Primary genomic-stability outcome metric evaluated in the comparative analysis, recorded as the response variable used to compare conditions; examples include aberration_burden, variant_count, or stable_line_fraction.

Name of the statistical test or model used to assess condition-dependent differences in the integrated table, recorded as the inferential method applied in this process step; examples include ANOVA, linear_model, or mixed_effects_model.
Method used to correct for multiple comparisons in the comparative analysis, recorded as the statistical adjustment applied to p-values or model outputs.

P-value threshold used to declare condition-dependent effects significant in the comparative analysis, measured as the cutoff applied to infer genomic-stability differences; typical values are between 0 and 1.

Criterion used to identify optimal maintenance conditions from the comparative analysis, recorded as the objective function or rule used to rank culture conditions; examples include minimum_aberration_burden or maximum_stability_score.
Date and time when the comparative analysis began, recorded for the computational evaluation step on the integrated metadata table.
Date and time when the comparative analysis completed, recorded for the computational evaluation step on the integrated metadata table.

stability_results.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only the computed comparative-result fields produced by the stability analysis: result identity, link to the analysis process, condition compared, key stability summary metrics, ranking, recommended condition, and confidence/interpretive flags. I excluded upstream integrated-table contents and the statistical settings used to generate the comparison because those belong to the Process and prior Derivative nodes. I also avoided all previously generated field names from earlier DAG steps, including generic timestamps and genome-build terms, to prevent collisions. The schema is focused on the final scientific output a downstream user would need to interpret which culture conditions best preserve genomic stability.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the final comparative stability result record; use a stable string format such as 'STAB_RES_01'.

Identifier of the comparative analysis process that generated this result, used to link the derivative output back to the computational process instance; use a stable string format such as 'COMP_PROC_01'.

Label for the culture condition or maintenance regime summarized in this result, recorded as the condition being compared in the final output; examples include a media supplement set, oxygen level, or passaging strategy combination.

Rank of the culture condition relative to the other tested conditions in terms of genomic stability, recorded as an ordinal outcome where lower numbers indicate better stability if so defined by the analysis.

Computed overall stability score for the culture condition, summarizing genomic integrity performance in the comparative analysis; the scale depends on the analysis method and should be documented in the result description.
Summary measure of genomic aberration burden for the condition, such as mean aberration count, median event burden, or a normalized score derived from SNP and WGS calls.
Summary measure of sequence variant burden for the condition, such as the number or rate of WGS-derived variants observed under this culture regime.
Summary measure of phenotype change associated with the condition, recorded as the comparative result for observed cell-state differences; the scale depends on the phenotype summary method.
Whether this condition is recommended or preferred for maintaining genomic stability based on the comparative analysis output; record the final recommendation label or yes/no outcome.

Confidence or reliability score for the final comparative stability result, recorded as the downstream quality metric for the derivative output; scale depends on the statistical and ranking method used.

Short interpretive note summarizing why the condition was ranked as it was, including key genomic-stability observations or caveats; use this field for concise scientific interpretation of the final result.
